title: Realizing Kan fibrations and comparing Kan homotopy groups
statement: Use simplicial sets, horns, Kan complexes and realization as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and k-spaces as in [lem-coef-realization-finite-limits]. Call $p:X\to Y$ a Kan fibration if it has the right lifting property against $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ for all $n\geq1$ and $0\leq i\leq n$. A Serre fibration of k-spaces means a map with the right lifting property against $D^m\times\{0\}\hookrightarrow D^m\times[0,1]$ for all $m\geq0$. The realization of every Kan fibration is a Serre fibration; neither $X$ nor $Y$ is assumed Kan. For a Kan complex $K$, its simplicial components (vertices modulo the equivalence relation generated by edges) map bijectively to $\pi_0(|K|)$. For a vertex $x$ of $K$ and $n\geq1$, define $\pi_n^s(K,x)$ using simplicial maps $\Delta^n/\partial\Delta^n\to K$ sending the collapsed boundary to $x$, modulo the equivalence relation generated by based simplicial homotopies with cylinder $(-)\times\Delta^1$, with the group operation given by Kan horn composition. Realization gives natural group isomorphisms $\pi_n^s(K,x)\cong\pi_n(|K|,x)$, compatible with pointed simplicial maps.
